texts:
Paste your avatar's .glb or .vrm link, or upload the file, and it is saved to your account, its bones are mapped onto one canonical skeleton for our animation library, and it goes on any website with two lines of HTML.

three.ws/import/rpm

Finding the file: if an app loaded your avatar from a link, open your browser's developer tools, go to the Network tab, filter by .glb or .vrm, and copy the request URL. If you saved the file earlier, use the Upload File tab instead.

Whatever rig it came with, the idle and walk clips then play on it. VRM 0.x and 1.0 files keep their toon shading, spring-bone hair and cloth, and expressions, and voice or camera capture can drive the face.
Then give it a job. Make it an agent with its own page and a Solana wallet, or put it on your own site with <agent-3d body="my-avatar.glb" brain="free"> and it talks to visitors with no API key.
